raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Purpose On ROCm, every MiniMax-M3.1 decode layer runs the NVFP4 sparse decode attention, then a separate `_kernel` launch (the MXFP8 activation quant of its bf16 output, K = 2048 per TP4 rank), then the `o_proj` GEMM. In the profile of a real decode step (rank-0 profile windows at N=4 and N=16) that quant is 60 launches per step, ~4.4-4.6 us each (profiled, inflated ~1.6x). This PR adds an `fp8_out` variant of the FlyDSL sparse decode kernel (`m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode_*_q8`) whose final store writes E4M3 values and row-major E8M0 scales instead of bf16, and hands them to `o_proj` as a `QuantizedActivation` (same mechanism as #63637 for `qkv_proj` and the FFN fusion in #65478). ## How it works - Output layout: in the final store a lane owns head `n`, dims `32g..32g+31`, i.e. exactly one 32-element MX block, so the quantization needs no cross-lane exchange. With split-K (`splits > 1`) the last workgroup of a row merges the partials and stores O; the quant runs there on the merged O, so every 32-block sees the final values. - Arithmetic: it quantizes the *bf16-rounded* values the bf16 store would have written (`pk_bf16`), computes the block amax on their integer bit patterns and the E8M0 byte as `clamp(exponent_field - 8 + (mantissa > 0.75), 0, 254)` (448 = 1.75 x 2^8, so this is `ceil(log2(amax/448)) + 127` exactly, no log2/division), scales by the exact power of two `2^(127-sb)` and converts with `v_cvt_pk_fp8_f32` (RNE). Hence the output is bit-identical to `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the same kernel's bf16 output (not "more accurate": it is the same values, unlike the swiglu fusion in #65478). - The scale formula was checked on CPU against `_mxfp8_e4m3_quantize_torch` on 20,000 random bf16 blocks over ~2^60 dynamic range plus edge blocks (zeros, subnormals, 447/448/449, the 1.75 boundary and the value just above it): 0 mismatches. The whole kernel compiles for gfx950 for splits 1/4/8 (`FLYDSL` compile-only on CPU). Bit-exactness on MI355X: see Tests. - Gating: `fp8_out` is a compile-time variant; the bf16 kernel and all other callers are unchanged. The attention layer uses it only for decode-only batches (`num_prefills == 0`) in eager or full-CUDA-graph mode and when `o_proj` can take MXFP8 input (`_can_fuse_input_norm_mxfp8`); mixed batches, piecewise graphs and non-NVFP4 impls keep the bf16 path and the linear's own quant. ## Files `ops/nvfp4_sparse_decode/kernel.py` (epilogue), `host.py` (new optional `out_q`/`out_scale`; `output` may be `None` then), `sparse_attention_nvfp4.py` (`forward_decode_mxfp8`), `model.py` (`MiniMaxM3SparseAttention` NVFP4 branch + `_run_attention` keyword outputs), `tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode.py`. `host.py` is also touched by the open split-heuristic PR #65481 (different hunks: it patches cleanly with offsets). ## Tests (MI355X, gfx950) New in `test_minimax_m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode.py`: (1) N = 1,2,3,5,8,12,16,24 requests x 4/8 rows x 30K/150K/500K context at the default split choice, (2) every split count 1/2/4/8 x XCD on/off x 1/4 KV heads x 1/4/8 rows with padding requests and a wide magnitude range. Both assert bitwise equality of values and scales with `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the bf16 kernel output and that rows past the batch are untouched. Result: the 96 new tests pass, and the whole file passes (176 passed), i.e. the existing decode tests are unchanged. The `i8` scale store and the split-merge path were correct on the first run. ## Measurements Profile trace Before: After: Graph-replay microbenchmark (a small benchmark script; 200 back-to-back launches per graph, median of 15 replays; 8 rows per request, 16 heads per rank, MI355X, 1 GPU), us per launch. "bf16 + quant" is the current path (decode kernel then `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`). Context 150K: | N | bf16 kernel | bf16 + separate quant | MXFP8 epilogue kernel | saved | epilogue cost vs bf16 | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 10.34 | 12.56 | 10.57 | 1.99 | +0.24 | | 2 | 10.74 | 12.78 | 10.93 | 1.85 | +0.19 | | 3 | 10.82 | 12.91 | 11.02 | 1.89 | +0.20 | | 4 | 10.86 | 12.99 | 11.14 | 1.85 | +0.28 | | 5 | 11.56 | 13.66 | 11.90 | 1.77 | +0.34 | | 6 | 10.07 | 12.15 | 10.29 | 1.87 | +0.22 | | 8 | 10.27 | 12.39 | 10.48 | 1.91 | +0.21 | | 12 | 13.67 | 15.91 | 14.13 | 1.78 | +0.46 | | 16 | 13.84 | 16.09 | 14.31 | 1.78 | +0.47 | | 24 | 18.39 | 20.72 | 18.64 | 2.09 | +0.25 | 30K and 500K contexts give the same numbers within 0.1 us (saved 1.79-2.11 us at 30K, 1.81-2.04 us at 500K). The separate quant costs about 2.2 us in the graph; the epilogue adds 0.2-0.5 us to the attention kernel, so the net saving is 1.8-2.1 us per layer. ## End to end (MI355X, TP4, DSpark 7 drafts, 150K context, DBO off, `VLLM_ROCM_USE_SKINNY_GEMM=0`) Arms on the same installed tree, 5 repeats each: **S0** = a tree that already contains the FFN quant fusions of #65478 and the routed-scale fold (so the baseline already has the other launch removals), **S2** = S0 + this PR; S0 was also run again at the end to check drift (S0 start and end agree within 0.14 ms at every N). **Profile window (rank 0, 60 steps, all streams), N=4 and N=16:** `_kernel.kd` (the MXFP8 activation quant) **82 -> 22 per decode step**, total kernels per step **1399 -> 1339 (N=4) and 1456 -> 1396 (N=16)**: exactly the 60 launches this PR removes; nothing else changes. **Decode step p50 (ms), median of 5 repeats** (noise of this benchmark about +-0.1-0.2 ms): | N | S0 start | S0 end | S2 (this PR) | vs mean(S0) | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 9.10 | 9.13 | 9.09 | -0.3% | | 2 | 10.04 | 10.05 | 10.00 | -0.4% | | 3 | 11.28 | 11.31 | 11.25 | -0.4% | | 4 | 11.65 | 11.53 | 11.66 | +0.6% | | 5 | 12.71 | 12.71 | 12.56 | -1.2% | | 6 | 13.08 | 13.10 | 13.13 | +0.3% | | 8 | 14.41 | 14.36 | 14.30 | -0.6% | | 12 | 16.01 | 16.15 | 15.85 | -1.4% | | 16 | 18.05 | 18.08 | 18.04 | -0.1% | The step-level change is small: negative at 7 of 9 batch sizes, mean -0.4% (about 0.05 ms), average -0.8% at N >= 12, but it is not separable from the noise at any single N. I therefore claim the exact launch removal and the per-launch kernel saving above, not a specific end-to-end gain. AgentX replay and GSM8K were not run (the epilogue is bit-identical to quantizing the bf16 output in the unit tests). ## Limitations gfx950 FlyDSL decode only; decode-only batches; K = 2048 per rank assumes 16 query heads per KV head with TP4 (generalizes to any heads x 128 since each block is within one head). AI assistance: this change was developed with Claude Code; the tests and benchmarks above were run on MI355X (gfx950). 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

nodes.body:
Thanks for the review. On your two asks:

**1. Decode-only and graph capture.** `_emits_o_proj_mxfp8` returns True only for a decode-only step: it needs `num_prefills == 0 and num_decodes > 0` in the sparse metadata and a runtime mode other than PIECEWISE. Prefill and mixed steps keep the bf16 output and the separate quant path. The cached `_o_proj_mxfp8` flag depends only on static module state (whether the impl has `forward_decode_mxfp8`, and whether `o_proj`'s kernel/quant key accepts MXFP8 input), not on the batch or on capture state, so it cannot flip mid-capture. The per-step part is re-read from the forward context each forward. FULL graphs are only keyed on uniform-decode batch descriptors in the cudagraph dispatcher, so a graph captured with the MXFP8 hand-off is only replayed for decode-only steps; mixed batches run PIECEWISE or eager, which take the bf16 path. In the decode profile (graph replay) the fused path is active. I have not added a unit test for the dispatch decision itself; happy to add one if you'd like.

**2. Multi-request / multi-XCD splits.** Added `test_decode_mxfp8_output_multi_request_xcd_splits` (2d8d5e5): DSpark 7 rows (8 per request) on the 8-XCD grid, explicit `splits` of 2 and 4, with 1, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17 and 24 requests, checking the fp8 output and scales bit for bit against `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the same kernel's bf16 output. The existing multi-request test (1-24 requests, 30K-500K context) runs at the default split choice, so it also covers whatever the heuristic picks once #65481 lands. #65481 is not in this branch, which is why the new test passes the split counts explicitly. All 110 MXFP8 epilogue tests pass on gfx950.
Thanks, this addresses both points. Please add the focused dispatch test as well: decode-only should use the MXFP8 hand-off, while mixed and PIECEWISE batches keep the BF16 path.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Looks correct on the fusion shape: quantizing after the split-K merge, one MX block per lane, and matching mxfp8_e4m3_quantize of the bf16-rounded store is the right contract for o_proj.

Two asks:
1. Please confirm `_emits_o_proj_mxfp8` stays decode-only (prefill / mixed steps still take the bf16 → separate quant path), and that a graph-captured decode step cannot flip the cached `_o_proj_mxfp8` decision mid-capture.
2. The bit-identical tests cover splits and heads — please also note (or test) the multi-XCD / multi-request path that #65481 retunes, so the fp8_out store is checked under the split counts we actually serve.

@@ -241,3 +241,104 @@ def test_decode_block_outer_pages_bitwise(num_kv_heads, decode_query_len):
     ]
     assert torch.isfinite(outs[0]).all()
     assert torch.equal(outs[0], outs[1])
+
+
+def _quantized_decode(q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, extra_rows=0, **kw):
+    """The kernel's MXFP8 output (values, scales) of the rows plus ``extra_rows``
+    sentinel rows that must stay untouched."""
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+        MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE,
+    )
+
+    k_scale, v_scale = _scales()
+    rows, heads, dim = q.shape
+    out_q = torch.full(
+        (rows + extra_rows, heads * dim), 0x5A, dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+    ).view(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+    out_s = torch.full(
+        (rows + extra_rows, heads * dim // MXFP8_BLOCK_SIZE),
+        0xA5,
+        dtype=torch.uint8,
+        device="cuda",
+    )
+    minimax_m3_nvfp4_sparse_decode_fly(
+        q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, SM_SCALE, None, k_scale=k_scale,
+        v_scale=v_scale, decode_query_len=qlen, out_q=out_q, out_scale=out_s, **kw,
+    )  # fmt: skip
+    return out_q, out_s
+
+
+def _assert_mxfp8_equals_quantized_bf16(q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, **kw):
+    from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization.utils.mxfp8_utils import (
+        mxfp8_e4m3_quantize,
+    )
+
+    rows = q.shape[0]
+    out_bf16 = _decode(q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, **kw)
+    assert torch.isfinite(out_bf16).all()
+    ref_q, ref_s = mxfp8_e4m3_quantize(out_bf16.view(rows, -1))
+    got_q, got_s = _quantized_decode(
+        q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, extra_rows=3, **kw
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(got_q[:rows].view(torch.uint8), ref_q.view(torch.uint8))
+    assert torch.equal(got_s[:rows], ref_s)
+    # Nothing past the rows is written.
+    assert (got_q[rows:].view(torch.uint8) == 0x5A).all()
+    assert (got_s[rows:] == 0xA5).all()
+
+
+def _assert_multi_request_mxfp8(num_reqs, qlen, ctx, **kw):
+    torch.manual_seed(num_reqs * 7 + qlen)
+    nb = (ctx + BLOCK - 1) // BLOCK
+    # Every request reads the same pages (read-only): a small cache at any context.
+    cache = torch.randint(
+        0, 256, (nb + 3, 2, BLOCK, 72), dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda"
+    )
+    for side in range(2):
+        sf = cache.view(nb + 3, -1)[:, side * 9216 + 8192 : (side + 1) * 9216]
+        sf.masked_fill_((sf & 0x7F) == 0x7F, 0x38)  # no NaN scales
+    lens = [ctx - 97 * r for r in range(num_reqs)]
+    table = torch.arange(nb, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda").repeat(num_reqs, 1)
+    seq_lens = torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    topk = _selections(lens, qlen)
+    q = (torch.randn(num_reqs * qlen, GROUP, D, device="cuda") * 0.02).bfloat16()
+    _assert_mxfp8_equals_quantized_bf16(q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, **kw)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("ctx", [30_000, 150_000, 500_000])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("qlen", [4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 12, 16, 24])
+def test_decode_mxfp8_output_matches_quantized_bf16(num_reqs, qlen, ctx):
+    """The MXFP8 epilogue equals ``mxfp8_e4m3_quantize`` of the same kernel's
+    bf16 output, bit for bit, at the default split choice for each batch."""
+    _assert_multi_request_mxfp8(num_reqs, qlen, ctx)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("splits", [2, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_reqs", [1, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17, 24])
+def test_decode_mxfp8_output_multi_request_xcd_splits(num_reqs, splits):
+    """DSpark 7 rows (8 per request) on the 8-XCD grid, explicit split counts
+    across the request ranges a split heuristic distinguishes."""
+    _assert_multi_request_mxfp8(num_reqs, 8, 150_000, splits=splits, xcd_count=8)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("splits", [1, 2, 4, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("xcd_count", [0, 8])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("num_kv_heads", [1, 4])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("qlen", [1, 4, 8])
+def test_decode_mxfp8_output_splits_and_heads(qlen, num_kv_heads, xcd_count, splits):
+    """Every split count (the last workgroup quantizes the merged O), XCD grid
+    and KV-head count; padding requests (seq_len 0) give zero values and scale 0,
+    like the quantized bf16 zeros."""
+    torch.manual_seed(3)
+    lens = [700, 0, 3000, 20000, 0, 129]
+    table, num_blocks = _block_table([max(s, 1) for s in lens])
+    seq_lens = torch.tensor(lens, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
+    topk = _selections([max(s, 1) for s in lens], qlen, num_kv_heads)
+    cache = _nvfp4_cache(num_blocks, _scales(), num_kv_heads)
+    # Magnitudes over many binades, so block scales cover a wide E8M0 range.
+    mag = torch.pow(2.0, torch.randint(-6, 7, (topk.shape[1], GROUP * num_kv_heads, 1)))
+    q = (torch.randn(topk.shape[1], GROUP * num_kv_heads, D) * mag).cuda().bfloat16()
+    _assert_mxfp8_equals_quantized_bf16(
+        q, cache, topk, table, seq_lens, qlen, splits=splits, xcd_count=xcd_count
+    )

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for the review. On your two asks:

**1. Decode-only and graph capture.** `_emits_o_proj_mxfp8` returns True only for a decode-only step: it needs `num_prefills == 0 and num_decodes > 0` in the sparse metadata and a runtime mode other than PIECEWISE. Prefill and mixed steps keep the bf16 output and the separate quant path. The cached `_o_proj_mxfp8` flag depends only on static module state (whether the impl has `forward_decode_mxfp8`, and whether `o_proj`'s kernel/quant key accepts MXFP8 input), not on the batch or on capture state, so it cannot flip mid-capture. The per-step part is re-read from the forward context each forward. FULL graphs are only keyed on uniform-decode batch descriptors in the cudagraph dispatcher, so a graph captured with the MXFP8 hand-off is only replayed for decode-only steps; mixed batches run PIECEWISE or eager, which take the bf16 path. In the decode profile (graph replay) the fused path is active. I have not added a unit test for the dispatch decision itself; happy to add one if you'd like.

**2. Multi-request / multi-XCD splits.** Added `test_decode_mxfp8_output_multi_request_xcd_splits` (2d8d5e5): DSpark 7 rows (8 per request) on the 8-XCD grid, explicit `splits` of 2 and 4, with 1, 5, 8, 9, 16, 17 and 24 requests, checking the fp8 output and scales bit for bit against `mxfp8_e4m3_quantize` of the same kernel's bf16 output. The existing multi-request test (1-24 requests, 30K-500K context) runs at the default split choice, so it also covers whatever the heuristic picks once #65481 lands. #65481 is not in this branch, which is why the new test passes the split counts explicitly. All 110 MXFP8 epilogue tests pass on gfx950.
Thanks, this addresses both points. Please add the focused dispatch test as well: decode-only should use the MXFP8 hand-off, while mixed and PIECEWISE batches keep the BF16 path.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Looks correct on the fusion shape: quantizing after the split-K merge, one MX block per lane, and matching mxfp8_e4m3_quantize of the bf16-rounded store is the right contract for o_proj.

Two asks:
1. Please confirm `_emits_o_proj_mxfp8` stays decode-only (prefill / mixed steps still take the bf16 → separate quant path), and that a graph-captured decode step cannot flip the cached `_o_proj_mxfp8` decision mid-capture.
2. The bit-identical tests cover splits and heads — please also note (or test) the multi-XCD / multi-request path that #65481 retunes, so the fp8_out store is checked under the split counts we actually serve.
